observations:
Torah #127 contains zero bechina-connected nodes and therefore zero packages can be proposed — neither existing-type nor new.

The criterion for a new package proposal is: 3 or more concepts with explicit bechina language forming an independent conceptual domain. Torah #127 has zero concepts with bechina language, making the threshold unreachable by definition.

The teaching consists of exactly two sentences:
1. 'הַבְּגָדִים הֵם בְּסוֹד הַחַשְׁמַ"ל, שֶׁהוּא שְׁמִירָה, וְעַל כֵּן הַבְּגָדִים יִהְיוּ שְׁלֵמִים תָּמִיד, וְלֹא קְרוּעִים, כִּי הוּא קִלְקוּל הַשְּׁמִירָה.'
2. 'הַבְּגָדִים בְּעַצְמָן תּוֹבְעִין אֶת הָאָדָם אִם לֹא נִזְהָר בִּשְׁמִירָתָן לְכַבְּדָן כָּרָאוּי וּלְהַחֲזִיקָן בִּנְקִיּוּת.'

The text provides an explicit cross-reference: '(עַיֵּן לְעֵיל בְּסִימָן כט)' — See above in Siman 29. This signals that Torah #127 is a dependent appendix, not an independent bechina-structured teaching.

Three candidates were examined for new package potential:

1. GARMENTS / CHASHMAL / PROTECTION (בְּגָדִים / חַשְׁמַ"ל / שְׁמִירָה): This is the most plausible candidate. The Rebbe draws a three-way connection: garments are in the mystery of the Chashmal; the Chashmal is protection; therefore garments are the protection-principle. If these three terms were equated via bechina language, they would form a small 'garments as protection' package with polarity 'good'. However: (a) the language used is 'בְּסוֹד' (mystical-correspondence), not 'בְּחִינַת' (bechina-equivalence); (b) 'שֶׁהוּא שְׁמִירָה' is a subordinate gloss on the Chashmal, not a standalone bechina declaration equating two concept-nodes; (c) the framework requires explicit bechina language as the threshold for package formation. The garments-Chashmal correspondence in Torah #21 (edge 1240: לבוש = חשמ"ל) is the closest dataset parallel, but that edge belongs to Torah #21, not #127. A new Torah #127 edge cannot be inferred from Torah #21's bechina structure. VERDICT: does not meet threshold — no bechina language, only be-sod language.

2. TORN GARMENTS / CORRUPTION (קְרוּעִים / קִלְקוּל הַשְּׁמִירָה): This pair represents the evil/defective pole — torn garments corrupt the protection. However, this relationship is entirely eitza (torn garments cause/constitute corruption of the protection). It is not a bechina declaration equating the two as parallel expressions of the same nature. There is no evil mirror package here because there are no good packages to mirror.

3. THE GARMENTS' CLAIM (תּוֹבְעִין): The idea that garments themselves hold the person accountable is a striking theological concept, but it is presented as a consequence (eitza) of the garment-shmirah relationship, not as a bechina identity. 'The garments claim against the person' is not declared to be 'an aspect of' any other concept via parallel-identity language.

CONCLUSION: The absence of bechina-type relationships in Torah #127 is a genuine structural feature of this teaching. Torah #127 is intentionally compact and referential — it points back to Torah #29 for its theological grounding. The Chashmal-framing adds a new kabbalistic dimension (the Chashmal as the metaphysical basis of garments-as-protection) but expresses it through be-sod language rather than bechina language, placing it below the threshold for package creation. NO_NEW_PACKAGES.
